tests: a spawn refuses an adapter that keeps the name set identical and restores a credential-store pointer, in two structurally different forms

consumesExternalOutput.provenance: The pointer half of the handover comparison (CR-B-001) is a CLASSIFICATION of another program's output: src/hooks.ts renders the turn-end hook, the adapter runs it as a child process, and src/spawn.ts turnEndEvidence parses the record it wrote and hands the env object to compareHandover. The capture at witness/captures/turn-end-hook-pointer-record.txt:1 is that hook's real output, taken 2026-09-18 on node v26.6.0 with env -i so the environment is exactly what is listed, in three arms: every pointer redirected, HOME reverted to /root with three pointers unset, and the pre-existing non-integer-argument arm which still exits 64 and writes nothing. HOW THIS WITNESS'S OWN NAMED TEST CONSUMES IT: the test reads the capture, asserts the three properties the kernel relies on (an env object, a reverted HOME recorded as a string, an unset pointer recorded as JSON null rather than omitted), and then RENDERS AND RUNS the hook live with HOME=/root, asserting the same contract against the file that run wrote, before it exercises the two reverting adapters. The two members are structurally different: member 0 writes NO observation at all, so the kernel falls back to the adapter's word and redirectionSource stops being child; member 1 writes an observation taken from the wrong place, so the guard runs and classifies something that is not the child's environment. An absent guard and a guard looking at the wrong thing are the two ways this defense fails.
